quiz.title: Grade 11 Trigonometry: Ratios on the Cartesian Plane
quiz.description: Test your understanding of coordinates, the terminal radius $r$, and the CAST diagram using localized South African contexts.

questions.prompt: A surveyor is measuring the elevation angle of **Table Mountain** in Cape Town from a base station. On their Cartesian mapping software, the line of sight to the mountaintop passes through the point $P(-5; 12)$ in Quadrant II. What is the value of the terminal radius $r$ and the ratio for $\cos \theta$?

During a night match at **FNB Stadium (Soccer City)**, a massive robotic spotlight rotates anti-clockwise, starting from the East touchline (positive $x$-axis) into Quadrant III (where $180^\circ < \theta < 270^\circ$). Which of the primary trigonometric ratios will be positive for any angle in this quadrant?

options.text: Sine ($\sin \theta$) only, because the South Stand is active.
Cosine ($\cos \theta$) only, because the commentary box is active.
Tangent ($\tan \theta$) only, because both $x$ and $y$ are negative, and $\frac{-y}{-x}$ simplifies to a positive ratio.
All ratios are positive in this quadrant.

questions.prompt: A container ship navigating off the coast of **Durban** has its radar locked onto a lighthouse. The navigation console shows that $15\sin\theta = -9$ and $\theta \in [90^\circ; 270^\circ]$. What is the exact value of $\tan \theta$ without using a calculator?

Sipho is solving a homework problem about a wind turbine blade in the **Karoo**. The tip of the blade is positioned at the coordinate $P(-24; -7)$ in Quadrant III. Sipho argues that because $x$ and $y$ are negative, the terminal radius must be $r = -25$. Why is Sipho's argument incorrect?

options.text: The radius is positive because squaring negative coordinates under the radical always yields a positive sum: $r = \sqrt{(-24)^2 + (-7)^2} = \sqrt{576 + 49} = 25$. As a distance, $r$ is a scalar and is always positive.
Sipho is correct because any value in Quadrant III must be negative.
The radius should be $r = \sqrt{-24^2 - 7^2}$, which makes it an imaginary number.
The radius is positive because $\tan \theta$ is positive in Quadrant III, which forces $r$ to be positive.

questions.prompt: A surveyor maps a circular water reservoir of radius $OP = 2$ units in a rural community in **Limpopo**. The terminal arm $OP$ makes an angle of $\theta = 300^\circ$ with the positive $x$-axis. What are the exact coordinates $(a; b)$ of the point $P$ without using a calculator?
